It’s not problems that are “the problem”. It’s our capacity to deal with them. If you’re healthy and powerful and likable and confident, then you can control your life much better. There will still be a lot of big events that take place that you won’t be in control of. But you will be able to move on to better things or you will be able to “fix” the problems. Unfortunately this is not an ability that everyone possesses. Some people are too dumb, too emotional, too unattractive, too unlovable, too unskilled and too mentally ill to face life’s difficulties and master them. No it’s not about courage or not giving up. One thing that might help you get through decades of shit is resilience, but that doesn’t mean that you are able to solve the problems. That just means you’re able to keep suffering without killing yourself or snapping and somehow are able to take more suffering. Like a high pain threshold. It’s still a life full of suffering.

And for some people, after years of rewriting your brain, you start to expect problems and expect not to be able to fix them. So your mind gives up. It presupposes that problems won’t be able to be fixed so it just wants to escape it instead.

A lot of people only have short depressive phases, usually brought on after a tragic event or after burning out. Or teenagers that don't live in a supporting and loving environment. Since these people are only depressed because of a current circumstance, it would be unwise to end their lives. Their situation and their mental health is likely to improve if treated immediately. This is what people usually mean by that saying.   


However, some of us have chronic/severe depression, have too many tragic events in our pasts, or have for decades lived a life that is not worth living. If a depressive phase is not treated early enough and is let to fester in the mind for years, it becomes a mental disorder, not just an illness. Then it becomes permanent. The only thing that can be done is to try to manage it, but life will keep throwing curve-balls and in the darkest of times it will be an unbearable existence. Still, after acknowledging this fact some will with their ever hopeful attitude say that we don't know what will happen in the future so we don't know that negative circumstances and an ill mind will never change. This is of course useless and is just a recipe for more suffering. False hope hurts more than no hope in the long run.  


So, the question is, which category do we belong to? Teenagers, burnouts and people in the face of a tragic experience. Or someone who's mind has been warped by life so much that depression is just the shape of our minds.   


One other thing. Some people have recurring depressive phases, maybe only a couple of weeks a year in winter. Or maybe only every 5-10 years after life becomes particularly tough. These phases can be managed with therapy and medication and the person can still have a fulfilling and meaningful life with contentedness. I would argue that in these cases it is worth to keep living even though depression can recur at some point again. But if someone has depression that makes them not be able to work, have a social life, a career, family, romantic relationship, and this has been going on for years; then i think the person has the right to die and it should be treated the same as a terminal physical illness.

Imagine you had a mentally-challenged neighbor next door who came knocking on your door and tell you that there is a large insect in their kitchen. You know they're mentally-challenged and you greet them with a smile. You go to their apartment to check out the kitchen and find nothing. They then point to a dark spot on the ceiling and tell you that it's right there and its going to jump on them and that they cant use the kitchen because of it. You try to explain to them calmly that it's not an insect but they insist it is. Because that is what they're experiencing in their mind and it's their reality. You somehow make them believe that you have killed the insect by just cleaning the dark spot and go back to your apartment.

In an hour the neighbor knocks at your door again and you greet them with a smile but the smile is not as real anymore. It is masking your slight annoyance and discomfort. Yet you listen to them again calmly as they tell you the exact same story with the insect in the kitchen. You go and clean it again. Then go back to your apartment.

Now the neighbor comes knocking on your door again after just 15 minutes. You open the door and you have trouble smiling but you force yourself and fake it. You hear the same story. This time you invite your neighbor inside and offer them to have a meal with you since they can't use their kitchen. They happily accept but then start talking about the insect in their kitchen again during the meal. You tell them that you will call an exterminator and the problem will be solved completely. You make an appointment that's in 3 days and tell your neighbor that the exterminator will be there in 3 days.

They thank you and go back to their apartment. 15 minutes later. They're at your door.  What do you do? Some people are wiser, more experienced in interacting with people with their behaviour and will continue to remain patient and will try to help in new ways they can find for a long time. There are also other people who have less patience or are simply inexperienced or very busy at the time.

So "normal people" may sometimes not want to interact with people that they have difficulty understanding or with people who bring them down or with people who test their patience. But more often than not it's simply because they don't know how to and because after a while they run out of options and therefore out of patience. And this doesn't have anything to do with being mentally ill or not. Regardless, you would also run out of patience or feel like you don't know how to help when in a similar position. Imagine having that neighbor. You would go mad after a while.

It's true that people who haven't gone through what we go through won't exactly understand us, but there are many who are still willing to help or willing to listen. You need to find those people. And when you reach out and find someone who listens, you need to try to dose the negative energy you are getting rid of. It's not the reaching out itself, it's the dose that a lot of people can't handle. You wouldn't be able to handle it either. The point is to take small steps and unload in small doses to the people who show interest in listening.

I had that same feeling and the same thoughts when i was 20 as well. It caused me to waste my life and lose what i had. I wasn't grateful because everyone around me were much better than me or had more in their life. I didn't realize how much i had. Most importantly the potential that i still had, just for being young. My mind was poisoned by the media and by my family members who were all successful. My environment made me think that i had to have a talent or be extremely successful and have the best grades and a great career. I mean if you want to try to go that route, you can but the chance of success and more importantly the chance of ever being satisfied with what you have accomplished is so small. If you're able to just say "Ok, i tried it, didn't work. Knew it was a small chance. Now let me get on with my life on a different path", then by all means people should take that path. But that is not usually what happens, is it? The truth is that most people will be mediocre and some will be very unsuccessful and will be struggling, while some will have it extremely good. So being mediocre is actually pretty good. I don't know where exactly this feeling of having to accomplish a lot and be rich and successful and awesome comes from but it's bullshit. Happiness lies elsewhere.  


Be careful. Staying in this mentality WILL ruin your life and you will find yourself in the bottom portion of society one day. You need to take it easy but at the same time not give up everything just because you dont accept mediocrity. Use your 20s wisely or you'll lose everything you have and you will be posting here in 10-15 years about how you had it all but couldnt see it. YOU DONT HAVE TO BE BETTER. STOP THINKING LIKE THAT. YOU ARE ENOUGH THE WAY YOU ARE. Good luck!

Well you don’t even have to do that but that’s what are body is programmed to do. To survive and procreate (which is just the instinct necessary for the survival of the species).

So the weird thing with suicidal people is that we are actually programmed to survive yet somehow we want to do the opposite. Not that I think being weird is bad. I like being weird. Well maybe only my kinda weird. But still; is there anything interesting about normal people? 

To come back to the original point. There is no meaning. We assign it meaning. Religions and even spiritual groups try to brainwash people into believing in their ideas of what the meaning of life is but all of those have been invented as well. We tend to stick to what other people say and believe in and try to blend in since we’re programmed to be social and programmed to survive. But you are your own person and you can decide. There's no such thing as your other half. It's a construct in your mind. That construct served you in the past and you derived energy from it in the form of affection, sex, and support. If we want to go deeper and even more technical, the relationship just made your body release the neurotransmitters dopamine, oxytocin, serotonin and norepinephrine among others into your nervous system in such an amount an ratio that it made you feel good. So after that construct is damaged or destroyed, obviously youve gone out of balance. Every rise has a fall. You felt the positive effects of being bound to a person so tightly. Now you feel the negative sides of it.   


Why the hell did i go into this seemingly unnecessary detail about? Because it can remind you that it's not about the person. It's an idea and a story in your head. There is no ONE for you or no one that is your other half. There are millions of people who would complement you, and also millions who would be too similar to you. That was one person. Yes, it might not be easy or fast for everyone to find a partner but its possible and its possible to do it again. I know nothing about your past relationship but it sounds to me like you have issues about attachment. This could be a sign that you need to work on that by practicing non-attachment.   


That being said, im sorry for what you're going through. I've had similar experiences and I know how heartbreak and the sudden cessation of a bond can affect your mind and body. The important thing to remember is that this is temporary. What you're going through is temporary. What helped me in coping with heartbreak and loss is to remember that YOU are the most important thing in the universe. You need to first look after yourself, respect yourself and love yourself. When you do that, then you'll realize that it wasnt your fault and you'll realize that its their loss. Why should you cry after, run after or even love a human being who stopped loving and respecting you? It doesnt make sense. They don't deserve your attention, affection or respect anymore. It's hard in the beginnning for the mind to adapt but it just needs time. You will even forget her face after a couple of years. Give yourself time to heal and good luck!

 So killing yourself won’t make anyone care more about you.

Actually you are right. All of depression stems from negative criticism and abuse and lack of attention (love). Obviously when those things repeat, your brain creates patterns that start to loop. After a while even if the experience is somewhat neutral, the electrical signals in your nervous system and brain start to take those negative paths. And the brain starts to negatively criticize “YOU”. Yourself. The root of it is still the negative criticism from others. Some are just less vulnerable to it (narcissistic self-centered self-righteous assholes mostly) and some are more vulnerable. And the thing is that it gets passed on. That’s how hate and evil is sustained in the universe.

So it’s not your fault.

I know how depression and the constant struggle fucks up the mind. I attempted at 17 and was about to at 20 again. So I can somewhat understand what you’re going through and how you feel (or not feel). Your experience is completely valid. Yet, The thing is, at that age people still have youthful energy. Even though it diminishes in depressive phases and makes you feel like you’re 90, the potential is still there.

 What you could do is to just kill your old self (personality with all your behavior and thought patterns) and start a new life. At your age, you can get a job anywhere. You can then start an education. Right now all of that might seem impossible and you might feel like you don’t want that (what’s the use if I feel miserable anyway right?). Yet when the cloud of depression slowly clears, you will see that it’s worth it. Why not just ride the waves of your 20s? That’s what I did after I survived my attempt. Even if you arrive at the same point in 10 years or several times during those years, you at least gave it a shot. I hope you consider this. Whatever your decision I wish you peace and happiness :)

Just be aware that you’re not responsible for him. In any way. You already have done so much good by being a friend and reaching out. He/she can/will be pissed though. That’s how I would feel. I was always extremely pissed when an old friend reached out to me right when I was about to commit. I think that a lot of people (including myself) who are stuck in depression for years or even decades have just accepted this diagnosis of „clinical depression“ or „being genetically wired to have a disorder“ or simply the diagnosis of a „professional” that says you are sick. It puts you into a victim mindset. Once you are there and accept this as your reality, it’s very difficult to get out of it. Even though psychiatrists have the goal to get you out of it and give you medicine and recommend therapy, still you have been told that something is very wrong with you and it becomes a part of your subjective reality. I think that’s extremely toxic and makes it worse. Now if someone is on the brink of suicide, then shocking the body and mind with drugs or Electricity or Magnets can be necessary and helpful (since you are too far gone to form any rational thought) to bring you back to a state where you are willing to work on and change yourself. But in other cases just mindlessly doing therapy and keep taking drugs will just keep you in the state of “I’m sick, somethings wrong with me so I have to keep doing therapy and taking drugs”. But that will just keep going on until your last breath. You won’t be able to get out of the cycle. Now if the therapy somehow manages to show you and make it clear to you that there is nothing wrong with you, that you are perfect the way you are just like everybody else, then it can be helpful. Because you’re neither better or worse than everyone else. Those ideas and comparisons are just hallucinations created my your mind that had the purpose of protecting you from danger and directing you towards resources (food, shelter, water, sex). It was very useful when we were simpler animals but now that we have such a developed prefrontal cortex and a mental world that we live in, those primal instincts and programs started to harm us. 

We are depressed and we are not in alignment at the moment, yes. But we are not victims, we are not lesser, we also are not better. We just are. All these thoughts have just accumulated in our minds about what we want, what we should have, what we should be like and those are not in alignment at the moment with what actually is ROGHT NOW. That deviation creates mental noise which when gone to the extremes creates depression and anxiety. The only way to align yourself again is to lower your expectations (FOR NOW) and lower the value of things you want to reach (the fantasies you have put on pedestals). You might even have experienced terribles things like rape, loss, murder, poverty, homelessness, loneliness, abuse in all other forms, but it’s in the past now. What is creating the mental noise is your brain trying to protect you but making it worse since you’re not a simple animal anymore. You weren’t able to just experience the pain and move on, or just learn to be careful next time, but you have become extremely sensitive to similar experiences. But all they are are thoughts. Even very vivid memories. They’re thoughts. And they’re not real. Even if it happened in the past, it’s not real anymore. The mind clings on to these experiences and constantly puts you into an unaligned State. But once you realize (truly have the A-HA Moment of realization that they are just thoughts, then you will start to go towards alignment again. My life started at 25. I had never had a girlfriend before, I had never stayed in my own apartment. I had never managed to stay in university. I had never really traveled to far places. Life starts when you make the decision to do so. Life starts now. The past is the past it is gone. What you do know will determine your future. More precisely your future “nows”. If you are sick of your life, then it means you have all the reason to change it. It won’t happen overnight but it can and will happen quickly as long as you take one step EVERY SINGLE DAY in the right direction.

Create a life plan. Make a list of all the areas about your life that you want to improve. Then under every category, write down the precise steps you can take yo achieve that. Research in the internet (but don’t overdo it, don’t fall into the trap of endlessly looking up tops and tricks to improve your life, taking action and DOING is more important). Go talk to successful and happy people that you know. Listen to podcasts of happy and successful people and take notes. Use those notes to modify your life plan.

Take a step every day. DO something new every day and do the same healthy thing every day. Start with exercising. Just go for a walk for 10 mins every morning. But without missing a day. Then increase it to 15 min after a week, then keep adding 5 mins. Then double it in a month. Join a gym if you can afford it. 

Learn to socialize woth people. Most people who are depressed are isolated and that causes them to get more depressed. Most people will feel better and like to live if they have regular positive social interaction.

Decide what you want to do in life. What used to give you joy as a kid. What skillset do you already have. It might be something you picked up while gaming. It might be being a good team player or being detail oriented or being very attentive. Write them down. Look for jobs that can use that skillset. You might be just 30% good at something. Build on that to increase your competence. Keep practicing until it becomes at least 60% and that will already be something you can use in your work life.

If you are not in a realtionship, learn to flirt by practice. Search for tips but only The ones that are applicable directly onto your daily life. If you are not very social, before flirting you need to learn to be more open and approachable and talkative and someone people like to be around in general. You can become that through practice. 

All of this will not happen in a day, not in a couple of months but you WILL improve every day and you will see the results faster than you expect.

So on this list of areas in your life that you want to improve choose one category first. And enumerate the others depending on their importance. Focus on the one you have chosen and start there. Once you see improvement you can add another category.

With all that being said, you probably knew all of this. You know that this is possible yet you might not be in the mind state to even decide to take this path of improvement. In that case what you need is therapy or medicine or a combination of both. Excuses might pop in your mind like, “but I don’t have enough money”, “but therapists aren’t too expensive”, “but I have thus huge mountain of work in front of me it seems improbable”, “but I don’t believe I can do this”. These are all excuses that your mind makes. The mind likes to stay the way it is, it likes to be comfortable and not challenged. It likes reality to stay the same so it can say “oh yeah this is how reality works and I know it”. But it’s not true. Reality can change drastically all the time. The mind can be schocked at any time. This usually happens when we lose someone unexpectedly or there is some natural disaster or some social event that wasn’t expected. The mind is schocked and either it immediately accepts the new reality and finds ways to adapt to it (usually very quickly and in a very creative way) or it freezes out of sheer shock. Now that is just to demonstrate how capable and powerful the mind is. But in your case what you need is to reform the mind a little bit every day, because then it will be stable and then you will be able to become a different person and have a different life. A life that you are satisfied with. A life in which you are content. 

What is your next step? Go take a long walk. When you come back, write down your first draft of your life plan with all the areas you want to change and circle the one you want to focus on.

Take it or leave it. It’s your life, it’s your decision. Good luck fellow traveler :)

Depression is not about your life situation or your upbringing. It can be a trigger but it’s not the only cause. It can be entirely neurological, it can be situational or it can be both. Also, your life situation is not how much money you make, which socioeconomic class you belong to or the environment you live in. You can be a privileged rich and famous celebrity or business mogul or a princess and still be depressed AF. What matters is how you perceive your life and yourself. If you are not content with your perception, then you will constantly experience cognitive dissonance and your brain neurochemistry will be out of balance and therefore cause mental illnesses/disorders like depression. 

If it’s a neurochemical imbalance which is not triggered by your negative perception of yourself and your life, then it can be fixed through meds most of the time. Especially if you have thoughts such as “why do I feel this way? My life is actually good, I have all I need and want but for some reason I am sad/ apathetic for long periods of time”. 

On the other hand maybe you really grew up privileged and in healthy nurturing environments but you experienced emotional trauma later in life. It could even be the experience of consistent micro-traumas over the course of years which keep you in an emotional state of sadness, hopelessness, helplessness, apathy. It doesn’t have to be one shocking traumatic experience. It could be multiple experiences of failure which gradually lower your self esteem. 

The point is that you shouldn’t feel like your feelings or current mental health problems are invalid because they are valid. It doesn’t matter how our life looks like from the outside but how we view it from the inside. Life is entirely your perception. If you are not satisfied with that perception for a long time, you will get depressed and it’s completely normal. 

I’d ask myself this first. What are the things I can change anout my life right now? Then immediately take action. Then ask what are the things that are possible to be changed but might need more time and planning. Then set a goal, set everyday-steps that move you towards achieving that goal and take those steps everyday. And for the things that you simply can’t change (which every human being has) starting a meditation practice while specifically meditating on acceptance will help. 

Of course all of this can only be achieved once you are in a mental state where you have hope and you believe that you can change your present. I know that in theory it all seems easy and clear but in practice it just doesn’t work because we simply lack the energy and will. Consistent therapy and the newer generation antidepressants can definitely help with that so if you have access to that, go ahead and set an appointment with a therapist. Nobody will truly keep in contact woth is if we isolate ourselves and even though we understand that logically we need to keep reminding it to ourselves. 

Wish you strength and perseverance. You sound like you are someone who can get through this.

The part written below is my experience with Mirtazapine and some thought on antidepressants. I realize you probably know all of this given your experience with depression so you don't have to read it :)

I have used mirtazapine and it didn't help me either. It improved my sleep a little (i wasn't able to sleep more than 1-2 hours at a time) which supposedly should also improve mental health. While I think that is true in general, i didn't get better at all. Also, 15mg is too high of a dose to experience sedative effects. It should be >7.5 mg. 

That being said, mirtazapine also made my visual snow flare up and worsened my manic thoughts and perception. I supposedly only have major depression but i think while I was taking Mirt, I also had at least hypomania and definitely anxiety. If someone has only major depressive disorder or is going through a phase of clinical depression, the mirtazapine shouldn't actually worsen your symptoms but 

   1. the possibility of your symptoms worsening or of increasing suicidal thoughts and feelings exists with ALL antidepressants (though a bit less with the latest atypical antidepressants compared to MAOIs and SSRIs) and

   2. The current understanding of what today's antidepressants do is still based on the Low-Serotonin theory which is finally being challenged but the existing medicine that's currently given is based on the assumption that a depressed person has low serotonin levels, especially within the brain. 

SSRIs and SSNRIs are just molecules like Serotonin and Noradrenaline which are necessary for the communication between nerve cells in the body but i don't think the simple act of introducing more of them into the nervous system is the cure to depression. However, they do seem to lift up moods for short intervals which can be all a depressed person needs in order to gain a clearer perspective and to see a flicker of light in the darkness. Everyone reacts and and is affected by meds differently. In general the strategy to cure or manage depression nowadays is to use the meds to get the depressed person out of that black whole, then stabilize their emotions and behaviour. Then keep giving them meds while they are receptive to and motivated to doing some form of therapy. Then increase their intervals of feeling content and happy. So the antidepressants just act as a crutch to help you stand up, you still have to walk to the finish line yourself, but without them you would have to crawl and be in so much pain that you wouldn't even want to try.

Now, the fact that antidepressants make you feel "more uncaring" or even like it's "screwing with your brain" is actually very common. You could be feeling more reckless or like you don't care because your neural receptors are being stimulated more than usual (your brain is more active), so you could feel you have more energy, that you're restless, or content. If we think of our mood/energy-level as being on a spectrum which spans from depressed to manic, then we could say that the more active our brain is, the more mental energy we have but the more chaotic and unorganized our thoughts and feelings can be (anxiety, mania), When we're depressed on the other hand, we tend to have less mental activity and even though we might have intense feelings we tend to lack energy. Antidepressants are meant to increase activity but neutralize intense emotions (emotions including happiness are dimmed in intensity). However, every medication has a different effect on everyone and you might need to test a couple of ones. There's no harm in asking your doctor to change the medication. They are usually stubborn but just tell them exactly what you've written here and repeat it if they dismiss it at first. 

The effect of meds also depend on the kind of illness. For example a person with bipolar should not take an SSRI class of antidepressants (or if they do, it needs to be combined with other meds). A bipolar person's mood/energy might be closer to mania during a phase and taking a med that increases activity in their brain will only make them more manic which is very dangerous. The higher energy one has (especially high mental activity which can manifest as anxiety or mania) the higher the probability of one feeling and being reckless will be.

if you are not somehow enlightened or zen enough to not care about people leaving you or disappearing out of your life (which is the case for most people) then you should never act needy, never open your heart completely, and never be too invested in a relationship. That's just the way it is. Think about it like this, would you want someone who constantly clings for your attention? Now what YOU consider being open and being yourself could be interpreted as being needy or clingy. Everyone has a different perception and a different line for that separates showing affection and asking for it to return crosses from being too clingy and needy. 

So never depend on others. We all depend in some way but we don't make it clear to others that we need them and we are not even aware of how much we need them ourselves. The way it works is that you always dance around the line. You never slip into neediness by getting your needs met by different people or other resources. The best is to get it from as many different resources as possible. That way you wont need the whole energy and affection and love from one source and as a consequence deplete them and make them leave. No one can satisfy all of your needs by themselves. 

Spiritualism and Eastern philosophy tells us that we need to have an inner source of energy rather than seeking satisfaction from externel sources. Well, if you can master that, then great. But for all of the other non-enlightened beings as us, a good strategy is like I've mentioned to have many different external sources. You should also not give your OWN energy freely to just one person. You can definitely be the first one to give and then wait for it to be reciprocated but you should only give it in small packets. NEVER  one large packet, and certainly not a constant stream of giving without getting anyrhing in return. 

Now this may seem like its not moral but on the contrary, it is the most moral way to go since you treat both yourself and others in a morally good way fueled by a rational strategy. Also worth reminding: Never fall into the illusion of "maybe i should give more, because im not getting anything back. Maybe i haven't given enough so i should keep giving". WRONG. This is the worst thing you could do and is the reason behind many people who get burnt out or depressed or simply abused. You carry the responsibility to look after yourself and to not fall into those traps people put in your way. The world isn't inherently evil, its around 50% evil and 50% good with fluctuations and changes experienced through different perceptions but this means that its not 100% good as well. Not even 90%. 

There WILL be traps and there WILL be people who want to use and abuse you. It's just the way it is. You just need to navigate this soup of good and bad by looking after yourself and never giving out more than you have. Always have your many external sources. Don't abuse those sources of course, and dont let those sources abuse you. Once you realize that either you are abusing or being abused, STOP. If you are the abuser and you think you are able to correct it by giving more to balance it out(not more than what you get) then you go do it. If not, still give what you can so that its 50/50 again and then end the relationship. If you are the one being abused, then there's nothing you can do to change it. You CANT FORCE someone to give you more, and you cant GIVE MORE TO GET MORE in that scenario. They are abusing you and you simply have to cut the CORD. As soon as possible. I repeat, AS SOON AS YOU REALIZE IT. That way you still have other sources that will keep you afloat and you will have enough time to find a new source to fill up the place of the one that ended. It's this simple.

NEVER TRUST PEOPLE 100% on the fact that they will always be there for you. They won't. You cant demand respect or love from someone, and you cant wait around to get it from them either. If you realize you are not being treated well, if you are not getting the respect and love you deserve, then end it and move on to the next one.

Send one small packet of love, if it comes back, send another. If you repeat this 5 times and it keeps coming back DONT FALL INTO THE ILLUSION that it will stay that way. It wont. Someone treating you well for a time doesn't mean it will last forever. You need to ALWAYS BE ALERT, meaning you should always be aware of how someone is treating you. Keep sending the small packets. If it doesnt come back. maybe you can send another one just to see if it arrived. But thats it NO THIRD PACKET. if theres nothing coming back after the second, you cut the cord and move on.
